cellStatuses.formalComposition: Neutral coprime ion ratio only; existence, stability and reaction feasibility are not established.
cellStatuses.literatureSupported: Only the claim in the annotated note is supported by the cited source and descriptive condition scope.
cellStatuses.excluded: Explicit legacy exclusion takes precedence; formal ion ratio is retained but formula is null.
cellStatuses.unsupported: Explicitly unmodeled chemistry or evidence scope; does not mean no reaction. Available for future annotations, with no current cells.

propertyReviewStatuses.propertyReviewed: Existing internal override record, not external certification.
propertyReviewStatuses.heuristic: Legacy property rules, not a measured property record.

validation: unique element, ion, annotation, condition and evidence IDs
positive finite ion masses and parsed atom composition
neutral coprime ratios for every ionic cell
override formulas conserve atom counts including conventional reordered formulas
exclusions precede overrides and return no generated formula
all nonexcluded cell formulas and ratios match the legacy generator
oxide coordinates use allowed element oxidation states
literature-supported annotations provide explicit scoped evidence
validationReporting: Counts describe deterministic data coverage, not chemical certification. Run DesktopLabBuild.ValidateOnly for current validation evidence; historical reports do not certify this change.
limitations: No universal existence or stability decision for formally balanced cells.
No new equilibrium constants, activity coefficients or quantitative precipitation thresholds.
Condition references describe evidence scope; ReactionConditionEngine separately enforces implemented reaction conditions.
Legacy colour, phase, solubility and hazard heuristics are retained for compatibility and are not comprehensively literature-reviewed.
Hydrates, coordination complexes and organic mechanisms are outside the formula grammar.
Separate oxide registry may use empirical rather than molecular formulas, such as P2O5.
